R1.rule: In comments, state only what the code cannot express, such as the why, a constraint, or a non-obvious fact.

R2.rule: Never write a comment that restates what the code does.

R3.rule: Use one sentence in a comment or message where one sentence is enough.

R4.rule: Do not write "now", "new", or "changed" in comments or messages.

R5.rule: Do not reference a session in comments or messages.

R6.rule: Do not include history in comments or messages.

R7.rule: Put history and the reasoning behind a fix in `.claude/plans/plan.md`, not in the code.

R8.rule: Write each docstring as one line, in the imperative mood, stating what the function returns or does.

R10.rule: Add a second docstring paragraph only for a real constraint or edge case.

R11.rule: In usage and help texts, state what the option does and its default, in under one line.

R12.rule: Do not include examples in usage or help texts unless the syntax is unclear.

R13.rule: Write errors, warnings, and skip reasons as the fact, the object, and the fix, in one line.

R14.rule: Name the real object, field, command, or limit in messages instead of vague references.

R15.rule: Do not use "some", "various", "etc.", hedges, or filler in comments or messages.

R16.rule: Use the same term for the same thing everywhere, with one word for one meaning.

R17.rule: Trim existing long comments when the code around them changes.

R18.rule: Do not trim existing long comments in a separate sweep.

R19.rule: Before committing, reread each new comment and message and cut every word that does not change the meaning.

R20.rule: Every agent must book a shared test environment (minikube or kees00) before using it.

R21.rule: Before any deploy, reset, chart test, test run beyond smoke or single reruns, or disruptive step on minikube or kees00, run the ledger check command for that environment.

R22.rule: Before any deploy, reset, chart test, test run beyond smoke or single reruns, or disruptive step on minikube or kees00, book that environment in the ledger with the agent, purpose, and time window.

R23.rule: Book the environment as soon as the work is planned, not when it starts.

R24.rule: When another agent deploys or rebuilds on your behalf, book your slot after theirs in the same step.

R25.rule: Book a deploy with the --disruptive flag.

R26.rule: Book a reset with the --disruptive and --resets flags.

R27.rule: During long work, send a ledger heartbeat at least every 20 minutes.

R28.rule: After the work finishes, mark the booking done in the ledger.

R36.rule: When adding a new component to the laptop environment, state its memory request/limit and its measured settled usage in plan.md.

R37.rule: Run one replica of every component in the laptop environment.

R38.rule: Use the smallest worker/process counts that keep behaviour identical to production.

R39.rule: Set heap sizes explicitly for JVM and Elasticsearch components.

R40.rule: Keep the production behaviour that tests depend on, such as auth, TLS, edge buffering and limits.

R41.rule: Shrink only capacity settings (replicas, heaps, pools, caches, retention), never production behaviour.

R44.rule: Run only the profiles that a given test needs.

R45.rule: When a change adds memory or CPU, propose ways to offset it before adding it.

R47.rule: Proactively propose savings with measured numbers, ranked by memory saved and by risk to production fidelity.

R48.rule: Never cut anything that the tests exercise.

R49.rule: When changing a memory-tuning setting, change only its capacity, never its behaviour.

R50.rule: Before changing a memory-tuning setting or adding a component, go through the memory-tuning checks.
